{{Short description|Mathematical theorem about the real analytic Eisenstein series}}
In mathematics, the classical '''Kronecker limit formula''' describes the constant term at ''s'' = 1 of a [[real analytic Eisenstein series]] (or [[Epstein zeta function]]) in terms of the [[Dedekind eta function]]. There are many generalizations of it to more complicated Eisenstein series. It is named for [[Leopold Kronecker]].

==First Kronecker limit formula==
The (first) Kronecker limit formula states that

:<math>E(\tau,s) = {\pi\over s-1} + 2\pi(\gamma-\log(2)-\log(\sqrt{y}|\eta(\tau)|^2)) +O(s-1),</math>

where

*''E''(τ,''s'') is the real analytic Eisenstein series, given by
:<math>E(\tau,s) =\sum_{(m,n)\ne (0,0)}{y^s\over|m\tau+n|^{2s}}</math>
for Re(''s'') > 1, and by analytic continuation for other values of the [[complex number]] ''s''.
*γ is [[Euler–Mascheroni constant]]
*τ = ''x'' + ''iy'' with ''y'' > 0.
* <math>\eta(\tau) = q^{1/24}\prod_{n\ge 1}(1-q^n)</math>, with ''q'' = e<sup>2π i τ</sup> is the [[Dedekind eta function]].

So the Eisenstein series has a pole at ''s'' = 1 of residue π, and the (first) Kronecker limit formula gives the constant term of the [[Laurent series]] at this pole.

This formula has an interpretation in terms of the [[Laplace–Beltrami operator|spectral geometry]] of the elliptic curve <math>E_\tau</math> associated to the lattice <math>\mathbb{Z} + \mathbb{Z} \tau</math>: it says that the [[functional determinant|zeta-regularized determinant]] of the Laplace operator <math>\Delta</math> associated to the flat metric <math>\frac{1}{y} |dz|^2</math> on <math>E_\tau</math> is given by <math>4y |\eta(\tau)|^4</math>. This formula has been used in [[string theory]] for the one-loop computation in [[Alexander Markovich Polyakov|Polyakov]]'s perturbative approach.

==Second Kronecker limit formula==
The second Kronecker limit formula states that

:<math>E_{u,v}(\tau,1) = -2\pi\log|f(u-v\tau;\tau)q^{v^2/2}|,
</math>

where
*''u'' and ''v'' are real and not both integers.
*''q'' = e<sup>2π i τ</sup> and ''q<sup>a</sup>'' = e<sup>2π i ''a''τ</sup>
*''p'' = e<sup>2π i ''z''</sup> and ''p<sup>a</sup>'' = e<sup>2π i ''az''</sup>
*<math>E_{u,v}(\tau,s) =\sum_{(m,n)\ne (0,0)}e^{2\pi i (mu+nv)}{y^s\over|m\tau+n|^{2s}}</math>
for Re(''s'') > 1, and is defined by analytic continuation for other values of the complex number ''s''.
*<math>f(z,\tau) = q^{1/12}(p^{1/2}-p^{-1/2})\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^np)(1-q^n/p).</math>
